label: Operating from itself: Operates x, a timeless primitive for immanent operation
term: operating from itself (the primitive Operates of SelfOperationLife)
definition: Operates x: x has an operation from itself (q.18 a.3 co.: operari ex seipsis, et non quasi ab aliis mota), an immanent operation that remains in the agent (actio quae manet in agente, q.18 a.3 ad 1), such as understanding. Explicitly identified PRIMITIVE: in Lean a parameter B -> Prop of SelfOperatingUnmovedLives, PureActOperates and NineOperate, constrained only by the open premises that use it. Distinguishing conditions: it is not motion (being moved or moving, DISAMB-MOTION); it is not transient action on another, unlike the broader operating-agent notion (DEF operating-agent, which includes transient activity); it carries no time index, unlike OperatesFromItselfAt (DEF-OPERATES-FROM-ITSELF-AT, its timed counterpart); and it is not life itself: life follows from it only through the open premise STMT-SELF-OPERATING-UNMOVED-LIVES, for what is also moved in no respect.
note: Stipulative analyst notion, attribution deferred; motivated by ST I q.18 a.3 (claim 611be1f0), which is not read as stating it. Open semantic obligations: a typed account of immanent operation (for example as an intellect or will in act with no potency, q.18 a.3 ad 1-2) under which the operation premises STMT-PURE-ACT-OPERATES and 'Whatever has the nine operates from itself' could be derived or fail; and how an operation without succession relates to OperatesFromItselfAt in a duration frame.
